reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 discusses a different alloy system and does not mention Y2O3. E2 provides general background on radiation damage and defect sinks but no specific evidence for Y2O3 in HEAs. E3 demonstrates benefits of TiC dispersoids in W, not Y2O3 in MoNbTaW. E4 shows processing challenges (oxide coarsening, Laves phases) in a related HEA but does not support the successful incorporation or benefits of Y2O3. The premises are thus largely unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Nano-scale Y2O3 dispersoids can be uniformly introduced into a refractory HEA matrix via mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will act as obstacles to dislocation motion, providing dispersion strengthening.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will pin grain boundaries, inhibiting grain coarsening at high temperatures.
Y2O3 dispersoids will serve as defect sinks under irradiation, enhancing point defect recombination and reducing damage.
The proposed processing can prevent dispersoid coarsening, which is critical for the predicted property improvements.
